signals.claim: By mid-June 2024, early peak-season demand, Red Sea diversions, port congestion and equipment shortages had tightened effective container-shipping capacity and pushed ex-Asia spot rates sharply above both spring levels and the initial Red Sea spike.

evidence.summary: Freightos reported Asia-US West Coast rates approaching $6,000/FEU, East Coast above $7,500, North Europe above $6,000, with early peak-season demand, Red Sea diversions, congestion and equipment shortages driving the move.

Xeneta said frontloading plus Red Sea capacity constraints and worsening congestion had already driven dramatic spot-rate increases, with further US East/Gulf labor risk potentially intensifying the squeeze.

contraryEvidence.summary: Part of the demand spike was explicitly attributed to frontloading ahead of tariffs, Red Sea delays and possible Q4 labor disruption, so some demand could be pulled forward rather than structurally new.

causalChain: Red Sea diversions consume more vessel-days and reduce effective network capacity
early peak-season/frontloaded cargo meets congestion and equipment shortages
spot freight rates reset sharply upward on transpacific and Asia-Europe lanes
container liners with large direct route exposure and operating fleet capture higher freight revenue as repricing reaches spot/short-contract cargo
incremental freight revenue has high operating leverage after voyage costs
signals.beneficiaryArchetype: A large container liner, not a port or generic logistics concept, with material transpacific/Asia-Europe exposure, substantial operating fleet, direct freight-rate sensitivity, enough spot/short-contract repricing to capture the June reset, strong liquidity, and valuation that does not already assume a pandemic-like rate regime.

opportunityAssessment.profitPoolChange: The disruption temporarily shifts economics toward vessel capacity owners as effective capacity tightens and freight rates rise.
opportunityAssessment.duration: Likely weeks-to-quarters rather than automatically multi-year; highly sensitive to Red Sea normalization, frontloading exhaustion, port congestion and new vessel deliveries.
opportunityAssessment.expectationGap: Q1 company data still reflected international unit revenue below the prior year even as transpacific revenue had begun to recover, while June spot rates had reaccelerated sharply.
opportunityAssessment.keyUncertainty: How much of the spot-rate spike reaches the company's realized blended rate, given contract mix and timing.

candidates.name: 中远海控
candidates.economicExposure: 2024 Q1 disclosure showed a 510-vessel container fleet with 3.1056m TEU capacity; transpacific and Asia-Europe were major revenue lanes and Q1 transpacific group revenue was already +21.16% YoY.
candidates.monetization: The company directly owns/operates container capacity. A June spot-rate reset can raise realized freight revenue as cargo reprices, but contract mix and lags mean spot indices do not flow one-for-one into earnings.
earningsBridge: effective container capacity tightens and spot rates rise
realized transpacific/Asia-Europe freight revenue per box rises as cargo reprices
incremental revenue flows through a high fixed-cost shipping network
container-shipping EBIT and cash generation rise
candidates.balanceSheetCycle: Q1 2024 cash was about RMB174.4bn and the business entered the shock from a much lower 2023 freight-rate base. Shipping remains capital-intensive and cyclical; new vessel supply and lease/fuel costs matter.
candidates.competitiveQuality: Scale, 510-ship fleet, Ocean Alliance network and direct presence on the affected routes give genuine economic capture rather than thematic adjacency.
candidates.priceExpectation: Deterministic pre-signal returns, raw close and approximate valuation will be added before Candidate/Watch is finalized.
contraryEvidence: Q1 international revenue per TEU was still below the prior-year level despite route-revenue improvement.
Frontloading can borrow demand from later months.
New vessel deliveries and normalization of Red Sea routing can rapidly restore effective capacity.
thesisBreakers: Red Sea routing normalizes and effective capacity returns quickly
June frontloading exhausts cargo demand and spot rates fall before contract repricing reaches realized revenue
new vessel supply or aggressive carrier capacity deployment overwhelms the temporary shortage
realized company freight rates fail to follow the spot indices enough to lift EBIT
unansweredQuestions: How much of the affected lane volume was spot or short-contract at the cutoff?
How much earnings upside was already embedded in the June share price?

pointInTimeEvidence.summary: Q1 2024: 510 container ships, 3.1056m TEU capacity, group cargo volume +10.53%; transpacific revenue +21.16%, Asia-Europe +6.53%; container-shipping EBIT RMB8.17bn; attributable net profit RMB6.755bn.

2023 annual report showed container-shipping revenue and EBIT had fallen sharply from the pandemic peak, with international revenue per TEU around USD1,055 for the group, providing a depressed cyclical base.

finalDecision.noTradeReason: Pending deterministic pre-signal price/valuation context. Economic mapping is strong.

signals.claim: China hog economics were inflecting sharply by mid-June 2024: official slaughterhouse procurement prices had risen roughly 5% week-on-week for two consecutive reported weeks while leading producers were simultaneously reporting falling full-cycle production costs.

evidence.summary: MOA monitoring for May 27-June 2 showed slaughter-enterprise hog purchase price RMB17.32/kg, +5.0% WoW and +13.1% YoY.
MOA monitoring for June 3-9 showed average hog purchase price RMB18.20/kg, another +5.1% WoW and +19.4% YoY.
Muyuan's June 6 investor communication said May full-cycle hog cost was about RMB14.3/kg, down RMB0.5/kg from April, driven by production improvement, lower feed prices and fixed-cost dilution.
Wens said May comprehensive hog-production cost had fallen to about RMB14.2/kg (7.1 yuan/jin), with 11 of 16 provincial units already below that level.

contraryEvidence.summary: Contemporaneous reporting noted renewed delayed slaughter and secondary fattening as prices rose, which could amplify near-term tightness but also create later supply and price volatility.

causalChain: prior sow/capacity liquidation reduces near-term slaughter supply
hog purchase prices rise quickly while feed/production costs fall
price-cost spread expands from loss/breakeven toward meaningful per-kg profit
large low-cost producers with high sales volume receive large operating leverage
cash flow and earnings can inflect before annual financial statements fully reflect the new margin regime
signals.beneficiaryArchetype: A large hog producer with direct and material hog exposure, high current sales volume, demonstrably falling full-cycle cost, sufficient liquidity to survive the downcycle, and a share price that has not already capitalized an unrealistically high long-run hog margin.

opportunityAssessment.profitPoolChange: Rapid expansion in producer margin per kilogram if observed market prices persist while feed and biological-production costs continue falling.
opportunityAssessment.duration: Cyclical, likely quarters rather than structural years; producer restocking and secondary fattening can later reverse the price signal.
opportunityAssessment.expectationGap: Q1 still showed losses for major producers, while May/early-June operating data pointed to a much sharper margin inflection than trailing earnings.
opportunityAssessment.keyUncertainty: How long high hog prices persist before supply response, and whether balance-sheet leverage offsets the earnings recovery.

candidates.name: 牧原股份
candidates.economicExposure: Pure/direct large-scale hog producer. May 2024 sales were 5.86m head and RMB10.45bn revenue; company selling price was RMB15.52/kg.
candidates.monetization: May full-cycle cost was reported around RMB14.3/kg and still falling, so a market price near RMB18/kg would create large per-kg operating leverage if sustained.
earningsBridge: industry hog price rises while full-cycle cost falls
large monthly slaughter/sales volume multiplies the spread
operating cash flow and net profit inflect from Q1 losses
candidates.balanceSheetCycle: Q1 2024 remained loss-making and leverage was high: liabilities about RMB125.1bn versus equity RMB71.6bn, short-term borrowings about RMB50.8bn, though cash was about RMB23.0bn and operating cash flow had turned strongly positive.
candidates.competitiveQuality: Scale and demonstrated cost decline are major advantages; the key quality test is whether the lower cost is durable across farms rather than limited to best-performing units.
candidates.priceExpectation: Deterministic pre-signal price and valuation context will be added before final classification.
contraryEvidence: Q1 net loss was RMB2.38bn and leverage remained substantial.
May company selling price was only modestly above its reported full-cycle cost before the June industry-price jump.
Higher prices can trigger delayed slaughter, secondary fattening and later supply response.
thesisBreakers: hog prices reverse before the price-cost spread is realized for enough sales volume
disease or production-performance deterioration pushes cost back upward
deleveraging/interest burden absorbs a large part of operating improvement
industry restocking rapidly rebuilds future supply and compresses margins
unansweredQuestions: How much margin recovery is already reflected in the June share price?
Can cost below RMB14.3/kg be sustained as volume remains high?

pointInTimeEvidence.summary: May sales: 5.86m hogs, RMB10.45bn revenue, company commodity-hog price RMB15.52/kg.
Q1 attributable loss RMB2.379bn, operating cash flow RMB5.067bn; quarter-end cash RMB23.0bn and liabilities RMB125.1bn.

candidates.name: 温氏股份
candidates.economicExposure: Large hog producer with 2.379m May hog sales and RMB4.66bn hog revenue, though poultry diversification reduces pure hog sensitivity.
candidates.monetization: May hog selling price was RMB15.83/kg while reported comprehensive hog-production cost was about RMB14.2/kg, giving a visible positive spread before the June official market-price acceleration.
earningsBridge: large monthly hog volume turns the spread into incremental gross profit
improved biological performance and lower feed cost support the spread
group earnings and operating cash flow improve
candidates.balanceSheetCycle: Q1 attributable loss was RMB1.236bn but improved sharply YoY; operating cash flow was positive RMB2.259bn. Liabilities were about RMB60.0bn versus equity RMB34.7bn.
candidates.competitiveQuality: Large integrated farming network and improving regional cost distribution; diversification into poultry lowers pure exposure but can reduce single-cycle concentration.
candidates.priceExpectation: Deterministic pre-signal price and valuation context will be added before final classification.
contraryEvidence: Hog exposure is diluted by poultry and other businesses.
The margin signal is cyclical and can reverse quickly.
Leverage remains meaningful and farming disease risk persists.
thesisBreakers: hog price rolls over before meaningful quarterly earnings capture
production cost stops falling or disease raises mortality/feed conversion
industry restocking rebuilds supply faster than expected
unansweredQuestions: Does diversification make the earnings inflection too diluted relative to 牧原?
How much of the recovery is already priced in?

pointInTimeEvidence.summary: May hog sales 2.3789m head, RMB4.66bn revenue, selling price RMB15.83/kg.
Q1 attributable loss RMB1.236bn versus RMB2.749bn a year earlier; operating cash flow RMB2.259bn; quarter-end liabilities RMB60.0bn.

finalDecision.noTradeReason: Pending deterministic pre-signal price/valuation context. Both candidates have a credible point-in-time margin bridge.

signals.claim: China polysilicon remained in severe oversupply in early June 2024: prices were near or below industry cost, inventories remained difficult to clear and producers were cutting/maintaining output while downstream demand stayed weak.

evidence.summary: InfoLink said buyer demand was decreasing, E&O inventory remained material, current shipment volume could not support price increases and inventory pressure would persist into Q3.
SMM reported widespread maintenance but June supply still above 140,000 tonnes; prices remained around RMB34-41/kg depending on grade.

contraryEvidence.summary: SMM also observed some downstream restocking and a short-term inventory decline, so the downturn was not assumed to worsen monotonically.

causalChain: excess upstream capacity + weak wafer demand -> polysilicon inventory pressure
prices fall toward/below cash-cost levels -> upstream margins compress and production is cut
lower raw-material costs could help downstream cells/modules
but downstream overcapacity and price competition can pass the cost benefit through to customers instead of shareholders
signals.beneficiaryArchetype: A downstream company that can retain falling silicon input costs as margin rather than immediately pass them through, with healthy end demand, differentiated pricing power and no large high-cost inventory.

opportunityAssessment.profitPoolChange: Upstream polysilicon profit pool is under pressure; downstream benefit is ambiguous because the whole PV chain is oversupplied.
opportunityAssessment.expectationGap: The negative upstream signal was already visible and broad; no clean long beneficiary was established.
opportunityAssessment.keyUncertainty: Whether any downstream company can retain input-cost savings rather than lose them through ASP competition.

finalDecision.noTradeReason: NO TRADE. The physical signal is credible, but the Skill cannot establish a clean long beneficiary with durable margin capture under broad PV-chain overcapacity.
